note: Phase 1 gate of the humour finishing run: 10 images from the 87-at-zero list, one per condition plus an extra wind, weighted to dusk/night. Al’s verdict calibrates or kills the run.

images.seen: A woman with a full basket on the lawn, three shirts on the line streaming dead horizontal in the wind, the Weber standing by at the wall under a blue Saturday sky.
images.why: one of the 87 photographs with zero lines after Al’s bank matching
lines: Everything on that line was dry ten minutes ago. The wind is just showing off now.
Two pegs a shirt today. Anything less is a donation to the neighbours.
This wind will have the washing dry before the coals are even grey.

images.seen: A Cape Town street at night, the palm streaming sideways under the streetlight, Table Mountain dark behind, the moon fighting through torn cloud, not a soul outside.
images.why: one of the 87 photographs with zero lines after Al’s bank matching
lines: The Cape Doctor is on night shift. The whole street has an appointment.
The palm is the only one still outside, and it regrets everything.
The southeaster doesn’t knock. You’ll hear it under the door all night.

images.seen: A gloved hand around a hot chocolate with marshmallows on a balcony over Camps Bay at sunset — and snow on Table Mountain and the Apostles behind it.
images.why: one of the 87 photographs with zero lines after Al’s bank matching
lines: Friday evening, snow on the Apostles, and the only queue is for the kettle.
Hot chocolate weather is self-diagnosing. The marshmallows are the second opinion.
Snow on the mountain. The kind of cold Cape Town frames and hangs on the wall.

images.seen: A lit swimming pool at night in steady rain, rings across the whole surface, the palm and the wall dark behind it.
images.why: one of the 87 photographs with zero lines after Al’s bank matching
lines: The pool is getting topped up for free tonight. Somewhere a water bill relaxes.
The only one swimming tonight is the rain itself.
The pool light is on for nobody. The rain appreciates the ambience.

images.seen: A father and his small daughter playing in the sprinkler at golden dusk, agapanthus in the foreground, the house lit warm behind them.
images.why: one of the 87 photographs with zero lines after Al’s bank matching
lines: The sun left an hour ago and took none of the heat with it.
Supper can wait. At this temperature the sprinkler promotes itself to family pool.
Officially he’s watering the garden. The garden is third in the queue.

images.seen: A farmhouse on open grassland with one grey column of rain coming down behind it, and a white plastic chair lying in the puddle by the road.
images.why: one of the 87 photographs with zero lines after Al’s bank matching
lines: The stoep chair made a run for it. It got as far as the puddle.
That grey column is someone’s afternoon getting cancelled. Ours is next in line.
Highveld rain doesn’t arrive. It gets delivered — all at once, one farm at a time.

images.seen: A school kid in a hi-vis vest waiting at the kerb in thick fog on a Monday morning, one faint set of headlights taking its time up the road.
images.why: one of the 87 photographs with zero lines after Al’s bank matching
lines: The fog swallowed the whole street and gave up at the hi-vis.
Those headlights have been ‘almost here’ for five minutes. Fog time runs slower.
Everything past the streetlight is a rumour until about nine.

images.seen: A cyclist paused on a winelands pass at dusk, looking up at a broken sky catching the last gold, the valley going dark below.
images.why: one of the 87 photographs with zero lines after Al’s bank matching
lines: Everyone’s an amateur forecaster on a pass like this. The sky isn’t telling.
The sky can’t decide between golden hour and going home early. Neither can anyone else.
Those clouds aren’t carrying rain. They’re just here to catch the light.

images.seen: A teenager railing a berm on a dirt track at clear golden dusk, the dust he’s kicking up glowing in the backlight.
images.why: one of the 87 photographs with zero lines after Al’s bank matching
lines: Golden hour turns even the dust into a special effect.
An evening this clear pays out its last hour in gold. Spend all of it.
Homework has extended office hours tonight. The sky said so.

images.seen: A hard-frosted lawn under a full field of stars, the house dark except one window, the bare tree black against the sky.
images.why: one of the 87 photographs with zero lines after Al’s bank matching
lines: Every star is out tonight, and the frost is the entry fee.
The Southern Cross is out, and so is the frost. Package deal.
By morning that grass will crunch. Beautiful night, expensive morning.
